annotation.title_clean: S.I. No. 563/2015 - Irish Aviation Authority (Small Unmanned Aircraft (Drones) and Rockets) Order, 2015
annotation.title_en: S.I. No. 563/2015 - Irish Aviation Authority (Small Unmanned Aircraft (Drones) and Rockets) Order, 2015
annotation.summary_en: Irish Aviation Authority order setting rules for small unmanned aircraft (drones up to 150 kg) and rockets in Ireland, effective 21 December 2015. It requires registration, restricts operating areas, distances and heights, mandates training for heavier drones and permission for the heaviest, and gives the Authority investigation and detention powers.
key_provisions_or_claims: Drones up to 150 kg must be registered as established by the Authority.
Operators must keep visual line of sight, stay below 120 m, and keep 30 m from persons and structures and 120 m from crowds.
Drones of 4 kg to under 25 kg need accepted safety training; 25 kg and above need Authority permission.
Flights in controlled airspace, restricted areas, or within 5 km of aerodromes require permission.
The Authority may investigate incidents, revoke permissions, and detain drones likely to breach the Order.
